questions: Did the unequal pupil size begin suddenly?
Have you had a severe headache or pain around the larger pupil?
Have you noticed double vision or drooping of the eyelid on the side of the larger pupil?
Have you had recent head or eye trauma?
Have you used any eye drops, scopolamine patches, or medications that could have contacted one eye?
Is the right pupil larger than the left in bright light?
Does the right pupil constrict better when focusing on a near target than when exposed to light?
Are the deep tendon reflexes in both legs reduced or absent?
Have you had abnormal sweating, dry mouth, constipation, or problems with heart-rate or blood-pressure regulation?
Have you had syphilis, diabetes, or a recent viral illness?
Does the right pupil intermittently enlarge or constrict over minutes, returning toward its usual size between episodes?
Do these episodes occur with headache or a personal history of migraine?
During an episode, does the right pupil become irregular or develop a sectoral “tadpole” shape?
Has the right pupil ever been documented to constrict to dilute pilocarpine?
Have you had recurrent episodes of blurred vision or eye pain in the right eye?
orders: Examine and document pupil size and reactivity in bright and dim illumination, including direct and consensual light responses and the near response.
Perform a slit-lamp examination for iris sphincter damage or pseudoexfoliation.
Perform a dilute pilocarpine (0.125%) eyedrop test in both eyes and reassess pupil sizes and near response after 30 minutes.
Perform a complete ocular-motility and neurologic examination, specifically assessing for ptosis, extraocular-movement limitation, and a relative afferent pupillary defect.
Perform 0.125% dilute pilocarpine testing in both eyes, followed by 1% pilocarpine testing if the dilute test is negative.
Perform  Apraclonidine 0.5% testing in both eyes and reassess for reversal of anisocoria.
served: deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses
lid position and measurement (MRD1 both sides)
